original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. docs/tasks/E16-adjudicator-hardening.md:27-28: the adjudicator imports no ERC-4626 interface and calls no exchange rate, and the forge tests check this as a source-level assertion.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. On integrated d51ae19, git grep over test/*.t.sol finds no ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares or preview. scripts/check-settlement-rate-free.py scans src/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.sol and src/nitro/ for these names; forge test does not run that script.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. 1. In armada-nitro at d51ae19 run git grep -nE 'ERC4626|convertTo|preview' -- 'test/*.t.sol': no output. 2. Run forge test and list the suites.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) armada-nitro forge suite (test/)
restatement: The armada-nitro forge test suite must itself enforce, by running real code, the rule that the adjudicator stays free of ERC-4626 exchange-rate machinery. Today that rule is checked only by the standalone script scripts/check-settlement-rate-free.py, which scans src/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.sol and src/nitro/ for ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares, and preview. forge test does not call that script, so a `forge test` run gives no signal on this rule at all; a future change could reintroduce one of those names into the adjudicator or the Nitro framework source and the forge suite would still pass. The fix must add a forge test that performs this same source check and fails the suite when a forbidden name is present, so that `forge test` alone is sufficient to catch a violation. The rule itself — that the adjudicator and Nitro source presently contain none of these names — already holds at commit d51ae19 and must keep holding.

restatement_clauses.text: src/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.sol and every .sol file under src/nitro/ contain none of ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares, or preview.
Running `forge test` executes a check for this rule and fails the suite when a forbidden name is present in that source, so the forge suite is itself the enforcement, not an unexercised side script.

goal: Make `forge test` itself fail if the adjudicator ever imports ERC-4626 or calls an exchange-rate function, instead of relying on a script forge test never runs.
acceptance_criteria: The adjudicator contract file and every file in the Nitro framework source contain no mention of ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares, or preview.

Running `forge test` passes against the real adjudicator source, but as soon as a forbidden name like convertToAssets is added to a scratch copy of that source and the suite is pointed at it, `forge test` fails. This shows the forge suite is the thing actually catching the violation, not a script it never calls.
